articles.title: Germany could scrap law banning insults against politicians
articles.description: Germany's special law prohibiting the insulting of politicians has led to cases that many people consider absurd. Some members of the government want to abolish the law; others think there's a good reason to retain it.

articles.title: Undav heroics help Germany beat Ivory Coast

articles.title: Terror police probe suspected anti-Muslim attacks in Edinburgh
articles.description: Counterterrorism police have taken charge after a series of violent attacks in the Scottish capital that left five men injured.

articles.title: Are Ukraine drones really exposing gaps in Russia's defense?
articles.description: Once seen as almost impenetrable, Russian air defenses are now under growing strain from Ukrainian drones. A recent attack on Moscow has reignited debate over Russian vulnerabilities.

articles.title: France bans alcohol during Fete de la Musique amid heat wave
articles.description: France is taking additional measures as millions of people gear up for Fete de la Musique under punishing temperatures.

articles.description: A court in Madrid ruled that there is sufficient evidence against Begona Gomez, the wife of Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez. The 55-year-old university director is banned from leaving the country.

articles.description: Ukraine's president has returned a medal to Poland after a decision to strip him of the country's highest honor. Warsaw has been one of Kyiv's key allies since Russia began its war in Ukraine.

articles.title: Inequality is elementary to Germany's school system
articles.description: Children's paths through Germany's school system are often determined before their first day of kindergarten, according to the national report on education. An elementary school in Bonn is offering a new model for kids.

articles.title: EU ban on BPA chemical in food packaging takes effect
articles.description: From July 2026 onwards, BPA will no longer be permitted in EU food packaging. The industrial chemical is known to interfere with the human hormonal system.

articles.description: Eva Maria Michelmann vanished in Syria in January as government forces advanced on Kurdish fighters in the northeast. The German government last week said it was working to get her home.

articles.description: Warnings of a mighty El Nino weather pattern this year could bring drought, flooding and extreme heat. Can we prepare for the worst of it?

articles.title: Baerbock: 'Germany team is an example to Germany's kids'
articles.description: The president of the UN General Assembly, Annalena Baerbock, praises the diversity of Germany's football team as it plays in the World Cup.

articles.title: How a feel-good German song is taking over social media
articles.description: Being encouraging and building confidence is what the German song "Gut genug" ("Good Enough") is all about. A meme is now bringing the track and its message to millions of people around the world.

articles.title: Why the Williams sisters and other stars are playing longer
articles.description: More than three decades after they burst onto the tennis scene, Venus and Serena Williams are still playing at the top level. Why are we seeing elite athletes carrying on into their 40s and beyond?

articles.description: Bavaria's regional domestic intelligence agency can monitor the right-wing populist AfD, the state's top court has ruled. Several states are trying to implement similar steps, with the opposition party challenging it.

articles.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has forged relations with Donald Trump, Emmanuel Macron, Keir Starmer and Giorgia Meloni. With some he is surprisingly close.

articles.title: Germany: 25 years since Nazi forced labor compensation began
articles.description: A German fund set up to compensate the millions forced to work for the Nazi regime is marking 25 years since the first payments were made. But for many victims, it was much too late.

articles.description: Talking, debating and listening are skills we can all learn, particularly in the light of current global conflicts. The Leipzig Bachfest shows how Johann Sebastian Bach's music can serve as a model here.

articles.description: Google's Debug research program plans to release millions of sterile mosquitoes to fight species that spread diseases like dengue. How does the method work — and should humans interfere with nature like this?

articles.description: Billions of euros sit untouched in dormant bank accounts in Germany. With heirs unaware and no central register in place, banks and politicians are debating who should ultimately control the money.

articles.description: Electric vehicles have taken off in Ethiopia. Key to the shift: a world-first ban on importing fossil fuel-powered vehicles.

articles.description: Xi Jinping is visiting North Korea for the first time since 2019. Pyongyang relies on China for 95% of its legitimate trade; hacking, arms deals and remittances also help it stay afloat.

articles.description: It started as a school project to promote local businesses in a remote Bavarian region. Now, the "Chiemgauer" currency helps to cut emissions.

articles.description: Two people were killed and transportation systems and businesses severely disrupted as Typhoon Lan lashed central Japan's Pacific coast after making landfall early Monday.

articles.title: Spotlight: U.S. decision to withdraw from UNESCO triggers calls for multilateralism
articles.description: The U.S. decision to withdraw from UNESCO, the UN cultural agency, has triggered worldwide calls for supporting multilateralism amid world challenges.

articles.title: U.S. nuke-powered submarine makes port call in S. Korea
articles.description: A U.S. nuclear-powered submarine on Friday made a port call at a city in southeast South Korea, Yonhap news agency reported Friday.

articles.title: S.Korean court extends detention of ex-president Park over corruption charges
articles.description: A South Korean court on Friday decided to extend the detention of impeached President Park Geun-hye who has been in custody and stood trial over corruption charges including bribery.

articles.title: Spotlight: What's behind abrupt U.S. withdrawal from UNESCO?
articles.description: The world has long been used to U.S. President Donald Trump taking a stance against multilateralism. Still, the sudden U.S. announcement Thursday to retreat from UNESCO -- the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization -- raised eyebrows worldwide.

articles.title: UN roots for enhanced data collection to fix food security crises in Africa
articles.description: The United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) will avail financial resources and technical expertise to help African countries collect data on agriculture that is key to addressing food security crises in the continent, an official said on Monday.

articles.title: Egypt-U.S. joint drill Bright Star simulates real battles
articles.description: Conditions similar to real battles were created in the Egyptian-U.S. joint drill "Bright Star 2017," which are being conducted at Egypt's Mohamed Naguib Military Base and will last until Sept. 20, local media reported on Monday.

articles.title: Cambodia arrests Laotian man with 5 kg of illicit drugs
articles.description: Cambodian police arrested a Laotian man on Saturday for allegedly smuggling nearly 5 kilos of crystal methamphetamine from Laos into Cambodia, an anti-drug police officer said.

articles.title: MPs say Brexit referendum led to public mistrust in government
articles.description: Actions by the British government during the European Union referendum led to public mistrust, a committee of MPs said Wednesday in a parliamentary report.

articles.title: S. Korea's ex-president Park arrested following impeachment over corruption scandal
articles.description: Former President Park Geun-hye of South Korea was arrested early Friday as a Seoul court approved the request from prosecutors following her impeachment earlier this month over a corruption scandal embroiling her.

articles.title: Manila Int'l Auto Show kicks off
articles.description: Visitors attend the Manila International Auto Show at the World Trade Center in Pasay City, the Philippines.

articles.title: Malaysia says to release body of Kim Jong Nam to DPRK
articles.description: Malaysia will release the body of Kim Jong Nam to the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK) and allow its nationals to leave, after the nine stranded Malaysian citizens in DPRK were freed, Malaysian Prime Minister Najib Razak said in a statement on Thursday.

articles.title: S.Korean court ends longest-ever hearing on warrant to arrest ex-president Park
articles.description: A South Korean court on Thursday ended the longest-ever hearing here on a warrant to arrest former President Park Geun-hye, who was impeached earlier this month.

articles.title: Federal judge in Hawaii extends order blocking Trump's travel ban
articles.description: A U.S. federal judge in Hawaii on Wednesday extended his previous nationwide order blocking the implementation of President Donald Trump's revised travel ban while the lawsuit continues.

articles.title: Kiev says ready for new truce with rebels in eastern Ukraine
articles.description: The Ukrainian Defense Ministry said on Thursday it stands ready for a new truce with independence-seeking insurgents in eastern regions starting from next month.

articles.title: Mixed reaction on London streets to British triggering Article 50
articles.description: The formal triggering of Article 50 by Britain to quit the European Union (EU) on Wednesday drew mixed reactions on London streets.
